questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It protects your entire face, not just your eyes.
It does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your entire face, not just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your whole face, including your eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good replacement for either one.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handles.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold both handles firmly and ease off the throttle. Use the brake on the tire that is not flat. Gradually slow down and move to the side of the road.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power comes from the front brake?

options.text: It should be the only brake used.

questions.explanation: The front brake provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader so experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: How can you increase your visibility as a rider?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on all the time. Also wear bright and reflective clothes, and change your position in the lane as needed.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: When the left arm is extended straight out to the left, it means the rider plans to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake pedal usually located?
questions.explanation: The rear brake pedal is usually located near the right footrest.

questions.question: How can you discourage other drivers from sharing your lane?

options.text: Give dirty looks to other drivers.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane leaves less space on both sides. This makes it harder for other drivers to try to share the lane with you.

questions.question: Where should you ride to be seen in a car's rearview mirror?

options.text: In the center portion of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane behind a car. This puts you directly in their rearview mirror, where drivers look more often than at side mirrors.

questions.question: Which formation keeps a group of riders closest together?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps the group close while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining in the body.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, they should:
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider waits until the first rider is safely back in the original lane before passing. Continue this pattern until all riders have safely passed.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Apply both brakes at the same time for a quick stop.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Change your lane position as conditions change.
Ride faster than usual to reach your destination quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight for better visibility.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position as conditions change.
questions.explanation: Be flexible about your lane position, especially at night. Use safe riding strategies when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Get the tailgater in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up only makes it more dangerous by increasing their speed too.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: When approaching a dangerous area like an intersection, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Either the front or rear brake, not both.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean with them. Sit as far forward as possible without getting in the way. Hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: If there are hazards on your left, you should ride:

options.text: On the left side of your lane.
On the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of your lane. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: When should you leave more space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: When it is colder than usual.
When you are following other motorcycles.

questions.explanation: Leave extra space between your motorcycle and other vehicles when roads are wet or icy. These conditions make it harder to stop. A two-second distance is normal, but you need more space on slippery roads.

questions.question: What should you NOT check before riding your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil, fluids, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn. You do not need to check reflectors during a pre-ride inspection.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to affect your ability to ride safely?
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your riding ability before you reach the legal limit. Even small amounts of alcohol can harm your skills. Never ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. These regulatory signs tell you the rules you must follow on the road.
